brief: Goldman's Quinn reads Commitment of Traders data covering August 18th to 25th. Non-Dealers sold $11.2bn of S&P 500 futures, ending a two-week buying streak, with long liquidation of $5.7bn and $5.5bn of new shorts contributing equally. Hedge Funds led at $15bn sold, $9bn of it long unwinds, the third straight week hedge fund liquidation ran alongside a rise in GS's Long / Short Stagflation basket, and the rolling three-month correlation between gross long changes and that basket turned quite negative. Quinn reads these categorical shifts as potential stagflation concerns. Asset Managers sold $3bn while Other bought $3.7bn and Non-Reportable $3.1bn. Afterwards solid NVDA earnings and guidance helped the S&P endure another jump in real rates from Jackson Hole and more Middle East fighting, yet futures flows still looked negative given the drop in funding. From August 25th to September 2nd the S&P fell 0.1% while the 10-year rose 12bp, the September S&P Adjusted Interest Rate BTIC shed 17bps and the December BTIC also declined, and the stagflation basket gained 0.9%. He offers growth versus inflation worries and/or stronger-than-expected month-end rotation as possible explanations, without choosing between them.
